name: PEG-MGF

b.x: PEG-MGF (PEGylated Mechano Growth Factor, also called PEGylated IGF-1Ec splice variant) is a modified version of a synthetic 24-amino-acid peptide. That peptide copies the last 24 amino acids of the MGF E domain (IGF-1Ec in humans). MGF is an IGF-1 splice variant that muscle expresses more of after mechanical loading [3]. The four references on this page cover native MGF or its E-peptide, not the PEGylated compound. That distinction matters. Native MGF is often quoted at a 5 to 7 minute half-life, but no published study has measured one. The attached PEG chain is meant to shield it from enzymes. The 48 to 72 hour half-life is an estimate from PEGylation principles, not a measurement. Community use centers on muscle recovery and satellite cell priming. Users inject 150 to 400 mcg subcutaneously or intramuscularly near the trained muscle, two to three times per week after workouts. Most consistent reports describe reduced delayed-onset muscle soreness starting around week two to three. The peptide is often stacked sequentially with IGF-1 LR3, with PEG-MGF running first to expand the satellite cell pool, then IGF-1 LR3 to drive differentiation. The honest assessment: PEG-MGF sits in a category where the underlying biology is real and the community experience is cautiously positive, but the clinical evidence gap is wider than for most peptides on this platform. Kandalla et al., with Goldspink, saw satellite cell activation in cultured human muscle cells [1]. Qin et al. mapped proliferation without differentiation in cultured porcine satellite cells [2]. A 2010 review by Matheny's group notes that no MGF peptide has been isolated from tissue or blood [3]. None tested the PEGylated form.

PEG-MGF binds to receptors on muscle cells through its unique C-terminal E-peptide domain. This binding activates quiescent satellite cells through a pathway largely independent of the classical IGF-1 receptor. The E-peptide down-regulates MyoD and p21, two transcription factors that normally push satellite cells toward terminal differentiation. By suppressing these signals, PEG-MGF keeps satellite cells proliferating without committing to become mature muscle fibers. This priming phase expands the pool of myogenic precursor cells available for repair. Think of it as building inventory. Once PEG-MGF levels drop after the cycle ends, mature IGF-1 signaling through the PI3K/Akt pathway takes over. That second wave drives the expanded satellite cell pool to differentiate and fuse into existing or new muscle fibers. The PEG moiety handles the pharmacokinetic problem. Native MGF is described as short-lived, but Goldspink's group gave no number [4]. The polyethylene glycol chain creates a hydration shell that blocks enzyme access. Small PEG chains still clear fast. In mice, a 6 kDa PEG left the blood with an 18-minute half-life [5]. The 48 to 72 hour figure for PEG-MGF is an estimate, not a measurement. Qin and colleagues mapped this proliferation-without-differentiation pattern in cultured porcine satellite cells [2]. Cultured human muscle cells in Kandalla's study [1] showed a similar activation signal. Neither study tested the PEGylated version directly.
PEG-MGF benefits center on satellite cell activation and post-workout recovery, with the strongest community signal in DOMS reduction.

Satellite cell proliferation without premature differentiation is the proposed core mechanism. In cultured porcine satellite cells, MGF boosted proliferation while blocking differentiation [2]; PEG-MGF itself is untested.
An estimated PEGylated half-life of 48 to 72 hours is why community protocols dose twice weekly. That figure has never been measured.
Community users consistently report reduced DOMS and faster session-to-session recovery starting around weeks two to three, based on 50 to 150 threads across r/peptides and peptide forums.
Localized injection near the trained muscle allows site-specific satellite cell activation. Intramuscular delivery maximizes paracrine exposure at the exact tissue that experienced mechanical damage.
Sequential stacking with IGF-1 LR3 covers both phases of muscle regeneration. PEG-MGF handles proliferation; IGF-1 LR3 drives differentiation and fusion into mature fibers.

Scientific Evidence
Based on 6 key studies · Research only
Zero peer-reviewed studies exist for the bodybuilding PEGylated compound specifically.
Dosing studied: No clinically established dose: community-derived 150–400 mcg 2–3×/week

All evidence is extrapolated from native MGF / MGF-E peptide animal and cell studies. PEGylation pharmacokinetics (48–72h half-life) are estimated from first principles, not measured. No formal human clinical trials have been completed for PEG-MGF. Human efficacy is entirely unproven.
Key Study

Kandalla PK et al. 2011, Mech Ageing Dev (PMID 21354439): MGF E-peptide lengthened the proliferative life span of human muscle cells from young donors, not old ones. Cited as most relevant positive result but studies native MGF, not PEGylated form.
Limitations

No human RCTs or PK studies for PEG-MGF specifically. All 4 cited references examine native MGF or MGF-E peptide in animal/cell models. The 48–72h half-life is an estimate extrapolated from PEGylation principles. Anti-PEG antibody formation risk is undocumented for this compound but is a class risk. Body of evidence does not support any efficacy claim in humans.
Community Experience
Cautiously positive for recovery enhancement and DOMS reduction; skeptical for direct mass-building effects.
Community dosing: 150–200 mcg 2–3×/week post-workout (beginner to moderate); up to 400 mcg 3×/week (advanced)
Valued over native MGF for practical twice-weekly dosing. Commonly used as a recovery layer within GH secretagogue stacks.

Science-Only Evidence

Community use is based entirely on extrapolation from native MGF animal data and PEGylation pharmacokinetic principles. No human study, positive or negative, of PEGylated MGF has been published. Community reports modest recovery benefit, but no scientific evidence (positive or negative) exists for this specific compound to align or diverge from. Classified science-only to reflect that any alignment assessment is based on indirect inference, not actual data.
Community Community dosing consensus from peptide research communities

Reconstitution math for a 2 mg vial with 1 mL bacteriostatic water: total volume is 100 units on an insulin syringe, each unit delivers 20 mcg. So 150 mcg is 7.5 units, 200 mcg is 10 units, 400 mcg is 20 units. For a 5 mg vial with 1 mL bacteriostatic water: each unit delivers 50 mcg. That puts 150 mcg at 3 units, 200 mcg at 4 units, 400 mcg at 8 units. Start at the beginner dose (150 mcg, 2 times per week) even if you've used other peptides before. PEG-MGF has zero human dose-response data; the community arrived at these numbers by trial and error over years, not from clinical guidance. Inject post-workout, within 30 minutes of finishing your session. The satellite cell activation window overlaps with the mechanical damage signal your muscles are already producing. For bilateral muscle groups (quads, pecs), split the dose between both sides. A single-site injection for bilateral training misses half the target tissue. Don't combine PEG-MGF and IGF-1 LR3 in the same injection window. Stagger them by at least 4 to 6 hours. Both compete for satellite cell receptor binding, and concurrent dosing may negate the proliferation phase. Store reconstituted vials at 2 to 8 degrees Celsius. Use within 3 to 4 weeks. Discard if the solution turns cloudy or contains visible particles.
Cycling Protocol
Cycle to prevent receptor desensitization. Most protocols use 4-8 weeks on, 2-4 weeks off. Inject on training days within 30 minutes post-workout for optimal satellite cell activation.
PEG-MGF Cycle

Community protocols cycle 4–6 weeks on / 4 weeks off based on presumed receptor accommodation within IGF-1/satellite cell pathways and to mitigate theoretical anti-PEG antibody formation risk. No human receptor desensitization data exists specifically for PEG-MGF. Cycling also limits continuous mitogenic signaling, which is prudent given the complete absence of long-term safety data in humans.
Diminishing recovery improvement during the cycle: DOMS reduction fades after week 3–4
Reduced muscle fullness or no further improvement in training capacity past week 4
Increasing injection site irritation, systemic fatigue, or unexplained inflammation over successive cycles
Possible anti-PEG immune response: injection site reactions worsening over time rather than improving
Gather supplies: PEG-MGF vial (2 mg or 5 mg lyophilized), bacteriostatic water, alcohol swabs, 29 to 31 gauge insulin syringe (0.5 mL or 1 mL).

Reconstitute by adding 1 mL of bacteriostatic water to the vial. Direct the stream against the glass wall, not onto the powder. Swirl gently until dissolved. Do not shake. For a 2 mg vial, this gives 20 mcg per unit. For a 5 mg vial, 50 mcg per unit.

Draw your dose Using a 2 mg vial with 1 mL BAC water: beginner 150 mcg = 7.5 units, moderate 200 mcg = 10 units, aggressive 400 mcg = 20 units. Using a 5 mg vial: 150 mcg = 3 units, 200 mcg = 4 units, 400 mcg = 8 units.

Clean the injection site with an alcohol swab For subcutaneous injection, pinch a fold of skin on the abdomen or outer thigh and insert at a 45 degree angle. For intramuscular injection near the trained muscle, insert at a 90 degree angle into the target area.
Inject slowly and hold for 5 seconds before withdrawing For bilateral muscle groups, split the dose between both sides (e.g., 100 mcg per quad for a 200 mcg dose).
Timing is post-workout, within 30 minutes of finishing your session. Inject on training days only, 2 to 3 times per week depending on your dosing tier.

Store the reconstituted vial in the refrigerator at 2 to 8 degrees Celsius. Use within 3 to 4 weeks. Lyophilized (unreconstituted) vials store at 2 to 8 degrees Celsius for up to 12 months, or at minus 20 degrees Celsius for longer-term storage.
Alternative Routes
IM (intramuscular, site-specific)
Standard community dose 150–400 mcg per injection

IM injection near the trained muscle maximizes potential satellite cell exposure at the site of mechanical damage. Split dose bilaterally for paired muscle groups (quads, pecs, biceps). Unlike native MGF, the 48–72h half-life allows some systemic distribution even from IM dosing.
SC (subcutaneous)
Same dose range; site-specific localized effect may be reduced vs IM

The extended half-life makes SC dosing significantly more practical than for native MGF: systemic PEG-MGF exposure and satellite cell activation occurs. Community commonly uses SC abdominal injection. Localized muscle-specific effect is likely reduced vs IM, but systemic satellite cell priming still occurs.
Works With
IGF-1 LR3
PEG-MGF drives satellite cell proliferation without differentiation; IGF-1 LR3 drives the full PI3K/Akt/mTOR differentiation cascade. Sequential use covers both phases of muscle regeneration.

PEG-MGF 200–400 mcg 3×/week post-workout × 4–6 weeks → switch to IGF-1 LR3 50–100 mcg once daily × 4 weeks. Stagger by ≥4–6h if used on same training days: do NOT co-administer in the same injection window.
BPC-157

BPC-157 addresses connective tissue, gut, and systemic healing via nitric oxide pathways. PEG-MGF targets satellite cell activation. Combined for injury recovery protocols: complementary mechanisms with no documented interaction.

Ipamorelin

Ipamorelin stimulates pulsatile GH release upstream; PEG-MGF acts downstream at the satellite cell level. Community uses GH secretagogues as a foundation with PEG-MGF to maximize the muscle repair and growth environment.
Ipamorelin 200–300 mcg SC 3×/day + PEG-MGF 200 mcg post-workout 3×/week; ipamorelin continues through PEG-MGF on and off phases.
Avoid
IGF-1 LR3 (concurrent same-window)

Simultaneous dosing in the same injection window may cause receptor competition at the satellite cell level. Separate by ≥4–6 hours or run in alternating cycles. Sequential use is a validated community stack: this is a timing precaution, not an absolute contraindication.
Exogenous insulin / sulfonylureas

PEG-MGF carries an independent hypoglycemia risk via IGF-1 pathway activation. Combining with exogenous insulin or insulin secretagogues produces additive glucose-lowering effects. Avoid co-administration unless under medical supervision with active glucose monitoring.
Glucocorticoids (prednisone, dexamethasone)
Glucocorticoids impair satellite cell activation and antagonize myogenic pathways, significantly reducing expected PEG-MGF benefit.

The biggest concern with PEG-MGF is the complete absence of human safety data. No clinical trial, no pharmacokinetic study, and no toxicology profile has been conducted on this specific compound in humans. Every safety assessment is borrowed from native MGF animal research, PEGylation class effects, and community self-reports. That isn't a reason to panic, but it means you're working without guardrails that exist for better-studied peptides. Cancer risk deserves attention first. PEG-MGF activates satellite cell proliferation through IGF-1 pathway signaling. Any compound that stimulates cell division carries a theoretical mitogenic risk. The peptide is contraindicated for anyone with active malignancy, a history of cancer, or pre-existing musculoskeletal tumors. This isn't a soft warning. Hypoglycemia is the most commonly reported acute side effect at higher doses. PEG-MGF activates the IGF-1 pathway, which has independent glucose-lowering activity. Symptoms include shakiness, sweating, and post-injection fatigue. This risk compounds when stacking with IGF-1 LR3 or exogenous insulin. Monitor fasting blood glucose at baseline, at day 7, and at the end of each cycle. Injection site reactions (pain, redness, swelling) are standard for a peptide administered subcutaneously or intramuscularly. These tend to be worse during the first week and settle as technique improves and sites are rotated. Water retention and joint discomfort show up in community reports, typically at moderate-to-aggressive doses. Localized muscle tightness or cramping near the injection site is reported during the first two weeks. Blood pressure changes appear occasionally but without a clear pattern. Anti-PEG antibody formation is the long-term unknown. Other PEGylated drugs, including pegfilgrastim and PEGylated asparaginase, have triggered anti-PEG immune responses in clinical use. Nobody has studied this for PEG-MGF specifically. Worsening injection site reactions across successive cycles, rather than improving tolerance, may signal antibody formation. Cycling off for four or more weeks between courses is the community's precautionary approach. Contraindications: active malignancy or cancer history, pregnancy or breastfeeding (zero safety data), active intracranial lesions or pituitary tumors, uncontrolled diabetes or severe hypoglycemia risk, severe hepatic or renal impairment, known hypersensitivity to PEGylated compounds, pre-existing musculoskeletal tumors. Stop immediately and seek medical attention if you experience signs of hypoglycemia, infection at the injection site, or worsening reactions across cycles.
Common Issues & Solutions
If no recovery improvement by week 3, reassess injection route: SC abdominal delivery for this localized peptide may reduce site-specific effect; switch to IM near the trained muscle.
If using IGF-1 LR3 on the same training days, ensure ≥4–6 hour separation: concurrent dosing risks receptor competition and negates the proliferation phase.
If experiencing hypoglycemia symptoms (shakiness, sweating, fatigue post-injection), reduce dose by 25% or inject after a carbohydrate-containing meal rather than fasted.
If injecting bilaterally (quads, pecs), split the dose between both sides: single-site injection for bilateral training likely misses one side and creates asymmetric stimulus.

If the cycle benefit fades earlier than expected (week 3 vs week 6), consider antibody formation or product degradation: extend the off-cycle to 6+ weeks; a fresh lot with a current COA helps rule out degradation.

PEG-MGF has no FDA approval for any indication. It carries a research-only regulatory status. No clinical trial has been registered for this compound, and no pharmaceutical manufacturer produces it under GMP conditions. The peptide is sold online labeled "for research purposes only" or "not for human consumption." Quality control is a particular concern with PEG-MGF. Confirming intact PEGylation requires mass spectrometry beyond standard HPLC purity testing. Community reports flag inconsistent purity across products. Only lot-specific third-party certificates of analysis with both HPLC and mass spectrometry results confirm what a vial contains. FDA moved PEG-MGF out of 503A category 2 on Apr 22, 2026, after its nominator withdrew it. That does not make it eligible for compounding, because it is not on the 503A bulks list. FDA says it plans to consult its compounding advisory committee on PEG-MGF before the end of February 2027. Athletes subject to drug testing should treat this as prohibited. WADA's 2026 Prohibited List names mechano growth factors (MGFs) under S2.3, banned in and out of competition. This content is for educational and informational purposes only. It does not constitute medical advice. Consult a licensed healthcare provider before using any peptide.

faqs.q: What's actually different between MGF and PEG-MGF: is the PEGylation just hype?
faqs.a: Not at all. Native MGF is described as short-lived, often quoted at 5-7 minutes, though no published study has measured it. The PEG chain is meant to shield the peptide from enzymes. The 48-72 hour half-life is an estimate, not a measurement. The peptide sequence is the same; whether PEGylation changes its activity has not been tested.

faqs.q: Should I inject PEG-MGF post-workout or on rest days?
faqs.a: Post-workout is recommended to hit the satellite cell activation window during muscle repair. But since PEG-MGF stays active for 48-72 hours, the timing is less critical than with native MGF. Most protocols call for injection within 30 minutes post-workout, no more than 3x per week, to avoid receptor desensitization.

faqs.q: Are there any human studies on PEG-MGF?
faqs.a: No, and this is the biggest caveat. All four commonly cited references study native MGF or the MGF-E peptide, not the PEGylated form. The 48-72 hour half-life estimate is extrapolated from PEGylation principles, not measured. PEG-MGF has never entered a formal clinical trial.

faqs.q: Could I develop antibodies to the PEG chain over time?
faqs.a: It's a real concern. Anti-PEG antibodies have been documented with other PEGylated drugs like pegfilgrastim and PEGylated asparaginase. Nobody has studied this specifically for PEG-MGF, but the risk isn't imaginary. Cycling off for 4+ weeks between courses is prudent and may help prevent antibody buildup.

faqs.q: Why does PEG-MGF feel more subtle than IGF-1 LR3?
faqs.a: Different mechanism, not a weaker one. IGF-1 LR3 fires up the full IGF-1R/PI3K/Akt/mTOR anabolic cascade for rapid hypertrophic signaling. PEG-MGF specifically targets satellite cell proliferation: expanding the progenitor pool without triggering differentiation. You'll notice improved recovery, less soreness, and better training frequency rather than an acute anabolic effect.

faqs.q: What is the recommended PEG-MGF dosage?
faqs.a: PEG-MGF dosing varies by experience level. Beginners typically start at 150 mcg 2x/week, moderate users at 200 mcg 3x/week, and aggressive protocols use 400 mcg 3x/week.
PEG-MGF typically comes in 2mg or 5mg vials. Add 1mL of bacteriostatic water to the vial. Use the free calculator for exact syringe units based on your desired dose.

faqs.q: What is the half-life of PEG-MGF?
faqs.a: The half-life of PEG-MGF is ~48-72 hours (PEGylated, estimated, never measured). This determines how frequently you need to dose for consistent blood levels.
